assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amine formation from a niche problem into a routine, general operation. It is among the most used bond constructions in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis, with ligand design as the conceptual core. This is molecule-making at its most consequential.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the catalytic, general, ligand-controlled versions through the 1990s and onward, and their ligand families underpin practice today. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is a real precursor, but it was stoichiometric in tin and limited, so a two-person prize is defensible. I recall this history but have not verified it here.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of heavy industrial and academic use, with a mature mechanistic understanding. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to credit Kosugi as a third laureate for the precedent tin-amide coupling.
Cross-coupling was recognized in 2010, which may make some members view this as an extension of a prized area.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Directed and ligand-controlled C-H functionalization changes retrosynthetic logic by treating ubiquitous C-H bonds as reactive handles with predictable site selectivity. It shortens routes to complex molecules, matching the step-economy criterion I care most about, and is used in late-stage functionalization in industry.
assessment.attribution: Yu's ligand-enabled Pd catalysis and remote/template selectivity are the most general advance; Sanford's Pd(II/IV) work and oxidative functionalization, and Daugulis's early directing-group arylations, are distinct foundational pieces. Hartwig and Smith (borylation) also have claims, so the allocation is contested and this field is crowded.
assessment.maturity: Broad adoption in academia and growing industrial use, but scope and robustness remain uneven and the field is still moving. Recognition is plausible but perhaps slightly early.
uncertainties: Credit is spread over many groups and distinct reaction manifolds (Pd, Ir borylation, Rh), so a clean three-person configuration is hard.
Industrial impact is less proven than for cross-coupling.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened radical and single-electron pathways under mild conditions, enabling bond constructions that were impractical before, and is now routine in discovery chemistry and process labs. The chemical novelty is real: new reactivity, not only a tool.
assessment.attribution: The 2008 papers from MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson are the usual triad, with Nicewicz, Fukuzumi, Konig and Melchiorre also contributing important strands. MacMillan already shared the 2021 prize for organocatalysis, which could push the committee toward other names. Attribution is genuinely open.
assessment.maturity: Very rapid adoption and independent confirmation across hundreds of groups, with industrial use in medicinal chemistry. Probably mature enough, though still evolving.
uncertainties: MacMillan's prior Nobel may make this triad unlikely; an alternative set would need to avoid him.
Ruthenium and iridium photocatalyst precedent from earlier photochemistry complicates priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolable stable carbenes overturned the view that carbenes are fleeting intermediates and created a new class of ligands and organocatalysts, with N-heterocyclic carbenes now central to metathesis catalysts, main-group stabilization and catalysis. The concept is simple and general, which I value.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand's 1988 phosphinocarbene came first, and Arduengo's 1991 imidazol-2-ylidene made the field general; both are core. Nolan and Rovis built the catalytic applications, so a third name is possible but dilutes the central discovery.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of confirmation and wide use. The discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Priority between Bertrand's earlier push-pull carbenes and Arduengo's crystalline NHC is a matter of interpretation.
Impact is mostly through downstream applications by others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation allows chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins from unprotected peptide segments, and expressed protein ligation extends that to large proteins. It is a clear chemoselective reaction concept with wide uses in protein chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson developed native chemical ligation (1994) with Muir contributing expressed protein ligation; Danishefsky, Brik and Liu add significant extensions. A three-person set is natural but not unique.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of use, confirmed in many total protein syntheses, though the practical effect is narrower than recombinant methods.
uncertainties: Impact may be seen as specialized relative to broader methods.
Danishefsky's competing ligation strategies make the credit boundary uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed metal-free reversible heterolytic activation of H2 and other small molecules, a conceptually new reactivity pattern that led to metal-free hydrogenation. It is clearly new chemically, though I question its practical reach so far.
assessment.attribution: Stephan's 2006 H2 activation and Erker's related intramolecular systems and later work are the credible pair; the credit is fairly clean.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many groups, but applications remain limited relative to transition-metal catalysis. It is still developing.
uncertainties: Substrate scope for catalytic hydrogenation remains narrow.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Intermolecular oxidative addition of alkane C-H bonds at iridium complexes was a landmark demonstration that saturated hydrocarbons can be activated by metals, and it set the conceptual stage for modern C-H functionalization.
assessment.attribution: Bergman's 1982 report is clear, but William Graham's contemporaneous work and later contributions by Jones, Periana and others are not in the credited names, so a Bergman-only prize may misrepresent credit. I cannot propose names outside the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and mechanistically understood, but the original systems are stoichiometric curiosities, and the practical impact came through later catalysis.
uncertainties: Graham and Jones, who made comparable discoveries, are not credited here.
A fundamental organometallic result rather than a general method.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom transfer radical polymerization gives controlled radical polymerization with defined architectures and has been widely used to make well-defined polymers. It is a practical general method that changed polymer synthesis.
assessment.attribution: Matyjaszewski and Sawamoto reported it independently in 1995, so a two-person prize is a fair split; Kamigaito and Wang add contributors. RAFT is a rival and parallel claim, which complicates the choice.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of use, with extensive confirmation and commercial applications, but it competes with RAFT and other CRP methods for recognition.
uncertainties: Overlap with RAFT (B015) makes it unclear which one the committee would honor.
Industrial impact is smaller than for cross-coupling.
